newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bond yields ended a quiet day steady, undeterred by a slightly worse-than-expected August producer price index figure.
Dealers said the market continued vulnerable to the upside and a test of the higher 15.40 percent level was possible over the next couple of days.
At 1417 GMT the R150 was at 15.37 percent from 15.38 percent at 1400 GMT on Monday after holding around the 15.38 percent level for much of the afternoon session.

"There was little reaction to the August PPI figure which came at the upper range of analysts' expectations. The market is generally nervous, people are unsure of direction and quite a few guys are long on stock," a dealer at a foreign bank said.

The Central Statistical Service said producer inflation rose 1.0 percent from July and was up 7.4 percent year-on-year. A Reuters consensus forecast of economists had predicted a 0.9 month-on-month and 7.2 percent year-on-year increase.
The dealer said the bias was towards further weakness with a break of 15.40 percent possible in a couple of days but bonds were likely to range-trade until then.
Others agreed that the picture was not too rosy.
"The rand is tending weaker and prospects of declining business confidence over the next few months are putting a dampener on the market," another dealer said.
The South African Chamber of Business said on Tuesday business confidence in South Africa was set to fall over the next few months as the country adjusted to slower economic growth.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners sold a net 160.44 million rand of South African bonds on Friday after buying a net 3.84 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 4.66 billion rand on Monday from 4.36 billion rand on Friday.
The rand ended slightly weaker on the dollar on the back of steady importer demand, currency traders said.
At 1415 GMT the rand was at 4.5335/5385 on the dollar from 4.5315/5365 overnight.
"We saw some dollars flowing in this morning but this was countered by steady importer dollar demand," a trader said.
Another expected the unit to creep up slowly to the 5.54 level during the week but noted that 4.5450 was the important psychological level which the Reserve Bank was likely to defend fairly strongly.
"The rand is looking vulnerable to the upside...there is still a continuous demand for dollars out there, both local and overseas," the dealer noted.
Against the crosses the rand was last trading at 7.0830/0954 from 7.0912/1022 at 1400 GMT on Monday and was at 0.3364/3369 marks from 0.3370/3375 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent, while 90-day BAs were slightly higher at between 15.20 and 15.40 percent from 15.20-15.35 percent.
The daily shortage was quoted at 8.405 billion rand on Monday from 8.032 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
